title.value: Part-based bird classifiers with an explainable, editable language bottleneck

abstract.value: Most CLIP-based image classifiers rely heavily on having known class names in the prompt and therefore are neither explainable nor editable to humans. Here, we present PEEB, a novel bird classifier that allows users to describe in text the 12 parts of every bird that they want to identify. After the textual descriptors are defined, PEEB detects 12 parts of a bird in the image and then computes a matching score between the image and each class by summing over the dot products of 12 pairs of visual and textual part embeddings. Besides editability, our classifier achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in two different zero-shot settings and competitive performance when finetuned on target datasets.

primary_area.value: representation learning for computer vision, audio, language, and other modalities
